(Links go to Google News feed pages; I could not resolve the original article URLs.)

## Market snapshot
1. **Midterms lift markets.** Democrats gained majorities in both the House and Senate. CNBC reports Dow futures up about 800 points, and Bloomberg says stocks and bonds rallied while the dollar fell. Early futures were mixed, with WSJ calling it a rebound. [CNBC](https://news.google.?oc=5)
2. **Fed holds rates.** On Oct. 28 the Fed left rates unchanged with midterms looming. A Reuters poll earlier showed nearly all economists expecting another hike in December. [ABC News](https://news.google.?oc=5)
3. **Fewer Fed votes.** Chair Kevin Warsh said the Fed will hold fewer rate-setting meetings: eight a year, with one 2027 meeting devoted to strategy and no rate vote. ## Advisor angle
With a December hike still widely expected and a firm job market, an advisor might spend client meetings on rate sensitivity: reviewing credit card and variable-rate debt and bond holdings. They could also explain why election-day swings in stocks, the dollar and gold are not a reason to change a long-term plan.

## Term of the day: FOMC
The Federal Open Market Committee is the Fed group that votes on interest rates. Warsh's plan means fewer meetings with a rate decision, so clients get fewer scheduled moments of rate surprise.

## Interview talking point
"The Fed held rates in October but markets still expect a December hike, and Warsh is cutting the number of rate-setting meetings, so I'd help clients plan around debt costs rather than react to each headline."
